title: AtlasCare Health Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
next_steps: Samir to share onboarding playbook and pricing sheet
Schedule technical deep-dive w/ SE and SRE for 2027-06-18
Customer to provide sample traffic profile and PII handling requirements
action_items: Samir Patel: Share onboarding guide, API quickstart, and pricing spreadsheet - due 2027-06-17
Lena Roberts: Run initial capacity estimate and recommend Dedicated vs Hosted profile - due 2027-06-18
Tom Ellis: Provide sample request/response sizes and peak qps from AtlasCare infra - due 2027-06-17
header: Date: 2027-06-15 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 60m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Roberts (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood CSM), Marta Diaz (AtlasCare VP Eng), Priya Sharma (AtlasCare Head of ML), Tom Ellis (AtlasCare SRE), Jenna Li (AtlasCare Product)
summary: Kickoff for AtlasCare onboarding to Redwood. High-level goals: migrate inference for triage assistant and clinical note summarization, clarify security/compliance needs (VPC, KMS, SOC 2), decide initial deployment (hosted vs dedicated), schedule technical deep-dive and benchmark pilot.
topics: Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everybody thanks for joining, um this is Samir from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. quick intros?
[00:06] Marta: hi i'm marta, vp engineering at atlascare, thanks for setting this up.
[00:10] Priya: priya here, head of ml. we run the clinical nlp team.
[00:14] Tom: tom, s r e, i'll be doing infra and security checks.
[00:18] Lena: lena, solutions engineer at redwood, i'll run the tech bits.
[00:22] Diego: diego, customer success. i'll help with onboarding timeline.
[00:27] Samir: awesome. goal for today — align on success criteria, deployment model, security requirements, and action items to get the pilot started.
[00:37] Marta: our big picture is to get the triage assistant live in q3 and migrate the note-summarization batch job later. latency matters for triage but summarization can be async. cost is... we have strict budget but also reliability for clinical usage.
[00:54] Lena: quick question on current infra, priya can you describe the model footprint and typical request sizes?
[01:00] Priya: sure, our main model is a fine-tuned llama-variant, ~30B pre-quant, we run quantized to 4-bit in prod. typical prompt ~800 tokens with 400 token response for triage, note summarization is 2k input sometimes. peak qps is around 15-20 for triage during surge windows, baseline is ~3-5.
[01:22] Tom: yeah and network wise we run in GCP us-east, we have VPC peering restrictions and need private networking for medical PHI. we can't send raw PHI to a multi-tenant hosted environment unless it's encrypted and contractually allowed.
[01:36] Samir: understood. we commonly see that. we support three deployment modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC/on-prem. for PHI-heavy workloads most customers start with Dedicated or Private depending on compliance.
[01:52] Marta: what's the cost delta typically between hosted and dedicated?
[01:55] Lena: it depends on utilization and batchability — hosted is pay-as-you-go so fine for low volume, but dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation. we've seen 30-60% unit cost improvement at steady high qps due to reserved GPU efficiency and caching.
[02:10] Priya: you mentioned caching — how does your prefix/K V cache work, does it keep context across requests?
[02:17] Lena: so we have KV cache and prefix caching; for repeated lookups (like forms) it can cache recent tokens to avoid recomputation, though for clinical notes with unique contexts it's less effective. KV cache is per-runner and we handle evictions based on age and usage. sometimes transcription shows K V as separate letters — but it's the same KV cache.
[02:38] Tom: regarding encryption and keys — we need K M S integration and customer-managed keys. any H S M options?
[02:45] Samir: yes we support KMS integrations and for Private we support HSM-backed solutions via partner integrations. we'll share our KMS docs.
[02:52] Marta: SOC two, iso, and audit logs?
[02:55] Diego: atlascare wants to see SOC 2 and syslogs, we have SOC 2 type ii, and we can provide audit logs per request.
[03:02] Samir: we'll attach our SOC 2 and ISO docs and a sample audit-log export. we'll also share our runbook for retention and redaction.
[03:11] Jenna: quick Q: SSO and RBAC for console access — we use SAML and SCIM.
[03:17] Lena: yep, SSO/SAML+SCIM are supported. RBAC can be scoped to teams and token-level controls.
[03:23] Priya: timeline — can we start a pilot next week, and run benchmarks end of next week?
[03:28] Samir: we can aim for initial pilot set up by June 22 if we get sample payloads and a security questionnaire back by June 17.
[03:33] Tom: i can send the request/response samples and a short network diagram.
[03:36] Tom: also need to know egress rules and whether there's IP allowlisting for dedicated.
[03:40] Lena: for Dedicated you get private endpoints and we can provide IP ranges for allowlisting; for VPC we do peering or private link depending on cloud.
[03:47] Priya: who will run the benchmark — redwood or atlascare?
[03:50] Samir: collaborative. Lena will set up the runner and initial model config, then we can run our standard throughput/latency tests against your sample traffic.
[03:58] Marta: for success metrics — triage latency 95th pctl < 450ms, accuracy measured by F1 on our test set with > 0.82 threshold, and cost target below $0.02 per call — are those realistic?
[04:13] Lena: 450ms 95p is aggressive for 800 token prompts on a 30B model unless you use model distillation/quantization and careful batching. on dedicated optimized infra we can get closer with lower context-lengths or using a smaller variant for triage. we should plan a tradeoff matrix in the deep dive.
[04:29] Priya: ok we'll add alternate SLAs if we need to reach a business outcome vs model parity.
[04:34] Samir: great. next, pilot scope: 2-week pilot, run triage path at 10 qps test, and note-summarization offline job for 5k docs. agreed?
[04:45] Marta: yes, 2-week pilot is fine.
[04:48] Tom: security questionnaire — i'll expect encryption details, key rotation, and data retention policies.
[04:52] Samir: will send an initial security pack and a short questionnaire; we typically ask for the customer to confirm PII flows.
[04:58] Jenna: product question — does redwood support function calling / structured outputs so we can map to our downstream systems?
[05:03] Lena: yes, we support structured output and function/tool calling in the hosted and dedicated runtimes. some transcription may show "function calling" as two words, but it's the same feature.
[05:11] Priya: and model catalog — can you pin model versions?
[05:14] Lena: yes, model pinning and rollout policies are supported; you can do canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a cheaper model if latency spikes.
[05:22] Marta: any blockers you foresee?
[05:24] Samir: main blockers are security sign-off and access to sample traffic. once we have those we can stand up a pilot environment. Diego will map the onboarding milestones.
[05:34] Diego: i'll follow up with a proposed timeline doc and invite folks to the technical deep-dive on 2027-06-18.
[05:40] Tom: minor note — we may need a clause for data residency in EU for some customers; atlascare has a EU clinic division but initial pilot is US only.
[05:50] Samir: noted. we'll include data residency options in the docs.
[05:54] Marta: ok wrap up, can you recap next steps?
[05:58] Samir: sure. recap: Samir to share onboarding playbook, SOC2/ISO and KMS docs; Lena to run capacity estimate and prepare technical deep-dive plan; Tom to share sample payloads and network diagram; Diego to schedule deep-dive (target 2027-06-18).
[06:15] Priya: thanks everyone.
[06:17] Samir: thanks, we'll follow up in email with links to docs and a calendar invite.
[06:22] Meeting end.
